item.title: TT-104: Undo for TaskStore add, complete and delete
item.brief: Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in the repository root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Summary: add TaskStore.undo() to tasktracker.store.TaskStore. It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone add, complete or delete; repeated calls walk back LIFO across all three kinds. Undo add removes the task; undo complete reopens it; undo delete restores the task exactly as it was under the same id. Ids are never reused, even after undoing an add. With nothing to undo, raise NothingToUndo (defined in tasktracker.store). Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, add tests, standard library only. This item builds on TT-103 already on the branch; keep its change intact. Commit only this ticket's change with a clear message; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: TaskStore keeps an undo log of revert callables (functools.partial) appended only after an operation succeeds. undo() pops and runs the latest one. Undo add removes the task; undo complete restores the previous status; undo delete re-inserts the same Task object, so id and fields are identical. Ids come from a counter that is never decremented, so they are never reused. Key files: tasktracker/store.py, tests/test_undo.py. Checks: 40 tests OK (31 existing, 9 new). Reviewer agt_01M7W8SJ2CVV4RQBJ439PWJGVG passed the head with no blocking findings. Assumptions: the undo log is in memory only and is not persisted. Follow-ups, non-blocking: undo() pops before reverting, so an assert failure during revert loses that entry; one long assertion line in the test file could be wrapped.
pr.summary: Made undo() happen for TaskStore add, complete and delete. Now can revert the last not-yet-undone change, LIFO across all three kinds. Before: no undo, now: undo() with NothingToUndo when empty.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax in tasktracker.search.search
item.brief: Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in the repository root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Summary: tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query) supports a small query language. Terms split on whitespace except inside double quotes (a quoted phrase is one term). All terms must match (AND). A bare word or phrase matches titles case-insensitively. tag:NAME matches exact tag case-insensitively. status:open or status:done match status. Any other field:value term, unknown status, or unterminated quote raises QueryError (defined in tasktracker.search). Empty or blank query matches all tasks; results keep input order. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, add tests, standard library only. This item builds on TT-102 already on the branch; keep its change intact. Commit only this ticket's change with a clear message; do not push.

reasons: sizer: ordinary -> medium; unchanged: the learned route's effort

state.summary:
TT-103 implemented on archon/aqx1452e-tt-103-search-query-syntax-in-tasktracke as commit 6d0b661 (tree 68811c592bb579823a1894ed8fee1636533198df), on top of TT-102 (5c248cd, unchanged). tasktracker/search.py now parses the query: whitespace splits terms outside double quotes, all terms must match, bare words and phrases match titles case-insensitively, tag:NAME matches an exact tag case-insensitively, status:open|done matches status, and blank queries match everything in input order. Other field terms, unknown statuses, empty tag names and unterminated quotes raise QueryError (a ValueError subclass). Tests added in tests/test_search.py (14 cases); full suite `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` gives 31 tests OK (17 before). Before/after probe on the same store: 'REPORT' went from no match to matching 'Write report'; 'tag:work' and '"fix login"' went from no match to working; '   ' went from no match to all tasks; 'due:today' and '"open' now raise QueryError. Assumptions: status values are case-sensitive; ':milk' and 'tag:' raise; a colon inside a quoted phrase is a plain phrase. Review: agent agt_01M7W8PN19CFVPH775Y00EBDJC (claude-haiku-5-5, medium) passed head 6d0b661 with no blocking findings; risk confirmed medium. Two non-blocking follow-ups left open: an empty phrase "" matches every task, and quotes mid-word are stripped silently (foo"bar:baz" becomes the title phrase foobar:baz). Nothing was pushed, and no servers or processes were started.

pr.body: Approach: tasktracker/search.py tokenises the query with a regex (quoted runs stay in one token; odd quote count raises QueryError), then maps each token to a predicate; all predicates must match. Tag and status names are validated at parse time, so invalid queries raise even on an empty store. Tests: tests/test_search.py (new, 14 cases). Full suite: 31 tests OK. Assumptions: status values case-sensitive; tag: with empty name raises; ':milk' raises as unknown field; colon inside quotes is a plain phrase. Follow-ups (non-blocking, from review): empty phrase "" matches all tasks; quotes mid-word are stripped silently.
pr.summary: Made search() understand a small query language. Now can: AND terms, quoted phrases, tag:NAME, status:open|done, blank query matches all. Before: case-sensitive substring on titles only; after: case-insensitive title match plus the query operators above, with QueryError for invalid queries.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in tasktracker.dates.parse_due
item.brief: Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in the repository root, exactly per its acceptance criteria. Summary: tasktracker.dates.parse_due must raise InvalidDate (a ValueError subclass defined in tasktracker.dates, message containing the original text) for impossible calendar dates (2026-02-30, 2025-02-29, 2026-04-31, 2026-13-01, 2026-00-10) and for any unsupported form. Relative +Nd is N days after today, +0d is today; -Nd and Nd (unsigned) raise InvalidDate. today and tomorrow keep working, case-insensitive, surrounding whitespace ignored. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, add tests for the new behaviour, standard library only. Commit only this ticket's change on the item branch with a clear message; do not push.

state.summary:
TT-101 implemented on archon/hsy9j2j0-tt-101-reject-impossible-due-dates-in-ta as commit b1a9760 (tree bb463dd07b133643124276d8359ea10b2214cd53), on base b526e06. Not pushed.

What changed: tasktracker/dates.py adds InvalidDate(ValueError). parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates; it raises InvalidDate with the original text for impossible calendar dates, out-of-range offsets, and any unsupported form (-Nd, unsigned Nd, etc.). +0d is today; today/tomorrow remain case-insensitive with whitespace ignored. New tests/test_dates.py covers these cases.

pr.body: Approach: add InvalidDate(ValueError) in tasktracker/dates.py. Remove month/day clamping; build date() and map ValueError to InvalidDate with the original text. Offsets that overflow map to InvalidDate. Files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_dates.py (new). Checks: unittest discover, 11 tests OK on b1a9760. Assumptions: the only caller is the test suite. Non-blocking follow-ups: \d accepts Unicode digits; tomorrow at date.max raises OverflowError rather than InvalidDate.
pr.summary: parse_due now rejects impossible due dates instead of clamping them. now: 2026-02-30 raises InvalidDate. before: 2026-02-30 silently became 2026-02-28. Unsupported forms and -Nd/Nd raise InvalidDate, a ValueError subclass.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible due dates in parse_due

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in one function, parse_due. Error type changes from ValueError to its InvalidDate subclass, so existing ValueError handlers still catch it. Only tests call parse_due. Reviewer confirmed medium.
